avoid: Exposure to open fires during drum tempering
Overly heavy instruments that strain the neck or shoulders
Sharp stick tips near the eyes or face
children.game_version: Call-and-response echo game: the teacher plays a short rhythm on the drum with a single foot stamp, and students mirror both the beat and the step in unison.

avoid: Deep knee bends and abrupt floor dips
Excessive continuous drum weight bearing without seated rests
seniors.counts: Count in steady 4-beat or 8-beat cycles, emphasizing the downbeat with a single foot stamp.
seniors.seated_version: Performers sit in a sturdy chair with the parai resting comfortably on the lap, practicing the three fundamental hand strokes with the Adi Kucchi and Sundu Kuchi while tapping heels gently on the floor.
seniors.standing_version: Perform stationary stamping steps with reduced knee flexion while the drum is secured with a padded nadai harness across the chest, maintaining an upright posture.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Maintain a steady, moderate tempo using slow Othayadi rhythms; keep foot lifts close to the floor without wide traveling steps.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Dominant hand manipulates the short stick near the lower rim; off hand rests on the upper frame maneuvering the long bamboo stick back and forth.
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stamping of the feet in synchronization with drum beats, walking transitions, and patterned floor steps resembling classical dance geometry.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Processional lines, circular group formations, and opposing ranks facing one another.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Swaying of the upper body and torso in coordination with drum strokes and foot stamping.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily standing and walking level, with variations executed in a seated position holding the drum in the lap.
movement_profile.partnering: Non-contact ensemble interaction; opposing lines trade contrasting beats and expressive postures in Parai Meala Koothu.
movement_profile.posture: Upright, dynamic stance with the drum suspended against the torso from a shoulder strap, permitting free leg movement and rapid weight transfers.

signature_moves.description: A direct strike to the center of the hide using the short, thick wooden stick held near the lower rim.
signature_moves.name: Adi Kucchi Center Strike

signature_moves.description: A slapping stroke delivered across the center of the drum using the long bamboo stick angled from above.
signature_moves.name: Sundu Kuchi Slap

signature_moves.description: Continuous alternating foot stamps coordinated with upper-torso swaying while maintaining continuous rhythmic drum strikes.
signature_moves.name: Synchronized Stamping and Sway

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Urgent, driving, and highly synchronized with intense percussive momentum.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid overheating the drum hide during fire tempering to prevent burning, black spots, or tears, which are considered bad omens.

music_profile.musical_form: Continuous percussive patterns with dynamic speed and emotional variations across 156 traditional rhythmic beats (adi).
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Derived from three fundamental stick strikes and structured around five primary meters: Othayadi, Thenmangu, Saamiyaattam, Thullal, and Uyirppu.
music_profile.sound_description: A sharp, explosive, high-pitched percussion sound produced by a fire-tempered animal hide frame drum beaten rapidly with a combination of a stubby wooden mallet and a flexible bamboo stick, punctuated by the shrill calls of the tharai woodwind.

basic_steps: Strap the parai over one shoulder using the nadai harness, securing the frame against the side of the torso.
Grip the Adi Kucchi (short stick) loosely between the thumb and fingers of the dominant hand near the drum's lower rim.
Rest the off-hand on the upper frame, balancing the Sundu Kuchi (long stick) between the fingers pointed downward.
Execute the center stroke by striking the middle of the drumhead with the short stick.
Execute the slap stroke across the drum center using the long bamboo stick.
Perform the compound stroke by striking with the dominant stick immediately followed by the off stick.
Stamp the feet rhythmically in place while swaying the torso in synchronization with the drum strikes.
Advance through spatial pathways while sustaining the rhythm in one of the five core meters such as Othayadi or Thullal.
teaching.formation: Processional lines, circular gatherings, or opposing lines facing each other (Parai Meala Koothu).
teaching.level_notes: Beginners focus first on the three basic striking strokes while stationary, then integrate foot stamping and weight shifts, before advancing to dynamic walking patterns and complex polyrhythms.
teaching.rhythm: Five basic traditional rhythms: Othayadi, Thenmangu, Saamiyaattam, Thullal, and Uyirppu, drawn from 156 traditional drum variations (adi).
